sentence_stem: Due to the sharp increase in energy prices,
full_sentence: Due to the sharp increase in energy prices, many households reduced their spending.
acceptable_variants: many households cut back on their spending.

options.text: however, many households kept spending freely.
options.why_wrong: 'However' introduces a contrast, but the sentence needs a result of the price increase, not a contrast with it.

options.text: because many households reduced their spending.
options.why_wrong: 'Because' repeats the cause already expressed by 'due to', creating a double connector.

options.text: so many households reduced their spending.
options.why_wrong: 'So' repeats the cause-effect link already made by 'due to'; only one connector is needed.

grammar_focus: Nominalization after 'due to' with a single cause-effect link
explanation: 'Due to' is followed by a noun phrase built on a nominalization ('the sharp increase'), so the sentence needs one main clause after the comma. Adding a second connector such as 'because' or 'so' is ungrammatical. Turkish speakers may add a second linking word here, carrying over the habit of marking the cause in more than one place.
translation: Enerji fiyatlarındaki keskin artış nedeniyle, birçok hane harcamalarını azalttı.
